title: Pinched cylinder: coarse octant
description: Cylinder radius 300, full length 600, thickness 3; E=3e6, nu=0.3.
geometry: 25 nodes; 16 elements. Cylinder radius 300, full length 600, thickness 3; E=3e6, nu=0.3.
material: E=3e+06, nu=0.3; shell thickness=3. Consistent benchmark units; displacements in deck length unit, forces in deck force unit, stress in force/length^2
boundary_conditions: Rigid end diaphragm and octant symmetry; quarter of unit radial point load at the symmetry intersection.
loading: Radial point force -0.25 in global X on the modeled octant symmetry corner.

references.citation: MacNeal, R.H.; Harder, R.L. (1985). A proposed standard set of problems to test finite element accuracy. Finite Elements in Analysis and Design 1, 3-20.
Ko, Y.; Lee, Y.; Lee, P.-S.; Bathe, K.-J. (2017). Performance of the MITC3+ and MITC4+ shell elements in widely-used benchmark problems. Computers & Structures 193, 187-206.

observations: The separately retained MH_pinched_cylinder_refined companion tests the same published target. Coarse-mesh error is displayed and is not relabeled as validation success.
limits: Linear elasticity and small-displacement equilibrium or linearized bifurcation/modal analysis; this is computational verification, not a material-test validation.
figure_caption: Recorded JFEM result; deformation is amplified, mode amplitudes/signs arbitrary. Green triangles mark constrained nodes; magenta arrows mark available point loads.
